page: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multi-threading enabled. It operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes a local storage allocation of 5669 GB NVMe SSD, while omitting dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position the E96ads_v7 in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng. Memory performance is similarly robust, with small-block read-only memory bandwidth and large-block write bandwidth ranking in the top 10%, while large-block read-only bandwidth remains strong in the top 25%. The system demonstrates exceptional processing capabilities in data compression, database operations, and Redis SET operations, all scoring in the top 10%. Additionally, the server achieves top-tier and strong performance marks in CPU-based LLM inference across small, medium, and large models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E96ads_v7 offers high resource density by combining a massive memory footprint with substantial local NVMe SSD storage on a single virtualized instance. This configuration minimizes the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads, optimizing resource utilization. The server is highly suited for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads, including large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data warehousing, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
